procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here for DM check. Says the holidays were "the usual." Fasting sugars 150-210 on the few days he checked. No hypoglycemia. No foot sores. Numbness unchanged. Eye exam in December stable per letter.

Vitals reviewed. Feet: skin intact, no calluses, monofilament reduced at toes as before.

A1c 9.0.

Plan: We talked again about adding something or titrating glargine. He is still reluctant; his main worry is lows. Gave him the titration plan in writing in case he changes his mind (raise 2 units every 3 days if fasting over 150, stop if under 100). Continue metformin 1000 BID, glargine 30, lisinopril, atorvastatin.
Return in April.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, patient at home with wife helping with the tablet. Identity verified with DOB. April visit cancelled when the office limited in-person care.

Doing OK. Staying home, wife does the shopping. Walking around the yard and down to the end of the road most days. Fasting sugars by his meter 140s-180s the last couple weeks. No lows. No new foot problems; he looks at his feet in the shower.

Meds unchanged, has 90-day supplies at home.

A/P: DM2, HTN, HLD stable by report. Labs deferred until the fall physical unless something comes up. He knows to call for any foot wound. Physical in October.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
64 y/o man, annual visit. Masked, first in-person visit since February.

Interval: has mostly stayed home this year. Less walking since summer. Eating more bread and rice than he'd like, admits. Fasting sugars higher, often around 200. No lows. No chest pain or breathlessness. Feet numb as before. Missed the FIT kit this year, says it is in a drawer.

Meds: metformin 1000 BID, glargine 30 qhs, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40. NKDA.
PHQ-2: 1 (a little down with the isolation, not most days).

Exam: well-appearing. HEENT normal. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart regular, no murmurs. Lungs clear throughout. Abdomen benign. No edema. Skin unremarkable. Feet: intact skin, pulses present, monofilament decreased at toes bilaterally, vibration decreased at great toes. Gait normal.

A/P:
1. Prevention: flu vaccine today. FIT: he'll find the kit and send it in.
2. DM2 with complications: labs today. Discussed again that if the A1c is still over 9 I would strongly recommend we raise the glargine.
3. HTN, HLD: continue.
4. Mood: situational, he and his wife are keeping each other company; will recheck at next visit.
RTC Jan/Feb.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Philip, your A1c is 9.6, the highest since you joined us. Kidney function is a little lower than last year (creatinine 1.31) but OK for now; we'll keep watching it. Cholesterol is fine. Urine protein normal.

I'd recommend raising your glargine using the plan I gave you in February: go up 2 units every 3 days while your morning sugar is over 150, and stop raising if any morning is under 100. Let me know what you think.

documents.title: RE: Your lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you doctor. I would like to try getting back to walking and less bread first. I will see you after new year and if it is not better we can do the insulin.

documents.title: Refill: glargine pens
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy request for glargine pens, 30 units qhs, 90-day supply, plus pen needles. Last visit 10/5, A1c 9.6. Refilled per protocol. FIT still not returned; reminder letter mailed.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Office Visit: Fatigue and Gait Change
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: tired, feet worse, walking is harder.

HPI: 64M with long-standing DM2 (since ~1996) with neuropathy and retinopathy. Wife made this appointment. Over the past several months he has been more and more tired, napping in the afternoons, which is new. The numbness in his feet has crept up and now he feels unsteady, "like walking on a mattress," worse in the dark. Pins and needles in his hands too, and in the legs above the usual area. Wife says he has been forgetting things: missed a dentist appointment, repeated the same story twice in a day. He thinks she is exaggerating but admits he lost track of what day it was last week. No falls yet. No chest pain, no black stools, no bleeding he's noticed. No alcohol. Diet: strict vegan for years, does not take a B12 supplement. On metformin since the late 1990s.

Meds: metformin 1000 BID, glargine 30 qhs, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40. NKDA.

Exam: pale, conjunctival pallor. Alert, conversant, but gave the date as the 8th (it is the 11th); knew month, year and place. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Neuro: strength 5/5 throughout. Vibration sense decreased in both legs to the ankles; joint position sense impaired at both great toes. Reflexes diminished at the ankles. Sways with eyes closed. Gait wide-based and cautious. Sensation reduced to light touch in a stocking distribution.

A/P:
1. Fatigue, pallor, new posterior column signs, memory lapses in a vegan on long-term metformin: B12 deficiency at the top of the list, with diabetic neuropathy contributing to the foot findings. CBC with smear, B12, folate, homocysteine, TSH, CMP drawn here today. Will call with results.
2. Gait: fall precautions reviewed; no driving at night until we sort this out.
3. DM2: A1c not repeated today, due next visit. Continue current meds for now.

Called lab at 5 pm: CBC back, Hgb 9.2, MCV 112, smear with hypersegmented neutrophils. Called patient, B12 pending, expect it tomorrow.

medications.sig: Inject 1 mL (1000 mcg) into the muscle daily for 7 days, then weekly for 4 weeks, then monthly

orders.order: Nurse visit: B12 injection and home injection teaching

documents.title: Results call: B12 deficiency
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Spoke with patient and wife on speaker. B12 118 (low), homocysteine 41 (high), folate normal, TSH normal. Together with yesterday's macrocytic anemia and smear, this is vitamin B12 deficiency with neurologic involvement. Likely cause is the long vegan diet without supplement plus decades of metformin.

Plan: cyanocobalamin 1000 mcg IM daily x 7 days, then weekly x 4, then monthly, long term. Nurse visit tomorrow for the first shot and to teach wife to give the rest at home; Rx for vials, syringes and needles sent. Explained the nerve symptoms may take months to improve and some may not fully recover. Recheck CBC in ~6 weeks. They agree.

documents.title: Nurse Visit: B12 Injection
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt here with wife. Cyanocobalamin 1000 mcg (1 mL) IM given L deltoid, tolerated well. Taught wife IM technique on the deltoid and thigh with return demonstration x2 using a practice pad; she will give tomorrow's dose and was confident. Reviewed schedule on a printed calendar: daily through 1/19, then weekly x4 (Wednesdays), then monthly starting late February. Sharps container provided. Wife has the vials from the pharmacy. Call with any questions.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up: B12 Deficiency
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Six weeks into B12 replacement. Wife has given every dose on schedule, one more weekly shot left then monthly. He says the tiredness is "half of what it was," no more afternoon naps most days. Hands tingle less. Feet still numb, walking a bit steadier but he uses the railing on stairs. Wife thinks his memory is better.

Exam: color better. Oriented x3, date correct. Vibration still reduced in the legs to the ankles, position sense still off at the toes. Gait still a little wide, steadier than January.

CBC: Hgb 11.0 (from 9.2), MCV 101 (from 112). Moving the right way.

A/P: B12 deficiency anemia, responding. Continue monthly IM after the last weekly dose. CBC, B12 and A1c in April. COVID vaccine: eligible soon with his conditions, encouraged to sign up at the pharmacy.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up: B12 Deficiency, Diabetes
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Monthly B12 shots now, wife gives them the first Monday of the month. Energy close to normal, he's back to his walks. Memory: no new episodes his wife has noticed. Hands no longer tingle. Feet numb as they were before all this, maybe a little worse at the toes. Unsteadiness much better, no falls. Both COVID shots done at the pharmacy.

O: oriented, conversational, tells a coherent history. Vibration reduced at the toes only now. Position sense intact at the ankles, slightly off at the great toes. Gait normal base, steady turn.

Labs drawn today, results by portal.

A/P
1. B12 deficiency anemia: clinically much improved. Continue cyanocobalamin monthly indefinitely (diet + metformin).
2. DM2: A1c drawn. He'd still like to try lifestyle first.
3. HTN: continue lisinopril.
4. BMP today.
RTC August for Welcome to Medicare visit.

documents.title: April labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Philip, good news on the blood count: hemoglobin is 12.4, nearly normal, and the red cells are back to normal size. B12 level is 690, right where it should be on the shots. A1c is 9.0, unchanged. Creatinine 1.42, a bit higher than last fall, we'll recheck in August. Keep up the monthly injections.

documents.title: B12 needles
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good morning. My wife says we are almost out of the small needles for the B12. We have vials left. Can you send the needles and syringes to the pharmacy? Thanks, Philip Hall

documents.title: RE: B12 needles
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Hi Mr. Hall, the syringes and needles were sent to your pharmacy this morning with refills for the year. They should be ready this afternoon.

documents.title: Ophthalmology Letter
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Dear Colleague,

Philip Hall (DOB 07/22/1956) returned 06/17/2021 for a diabetic eye exam; his 2020 exam was postponed during the pandemic.

VA cc 20/25 OD, 20/30 OS. IOP 15/16. Lenses clear. Dilated fundus: diabetic retinopathy OU, similar to 2019 photos. No macular edema on OCT.

Assessment: diabetic retinopathy OU without macular edema, stable.
Plan: annual follow-up.

Allergies: NKDA.

procedures.procedure: Initial preventive physical examination (Welcome to Medicare)

documents.title: Welcome to Medicare Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Initial preventive physical exam. Turned 65 last month.

Health risk review: lives with wife in a one-level house. Independent in daily activities, still drives in daylight. No falls this year. Hearing OK. Vision: eye exam June, stable. Exercise: walks 30-40 min most mornings. Diet vegan; taking B12 shots monthly now. No tobacco or alcohol. Seat belt always. Home has smoke detectors.
PHQ-9: 2.
Cognition: oriented, recalls 3/3 words, clock drawing normal.
Advance directive: his wife is his health care agent; form given to complete at home.

Interval: energy good. Feet numb, no wounds. No urinary or bowel complaints.

Meds: metformin 1000 BID, glargine 30 qhs, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40, cyanocobalamin 1000 mcg IM monthly. NKDA.

Exam: well. HEENT normal, neck no masses. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. No edema. Skin: no lesions of concern. Feet: skin intact, pulses 2+, monofilament reduced at toes, vibration reduced at great toes. Gait steady.

Plan:
- Labs today: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c, urine albumin.
- Vaccines: flu in the fall (high-dose now that he is 65). Pneumococcal and shingles vaccines to discuss at the fall visit. COVID booster when offered.
- Colon screening: FIT overdue, new kit given; he is open to colonoscopy "next year."
- Written screening schedule given.

documents.title: Results from your Medicare visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Philip, a few things from your labs:
- Hemoglobin 12.6, holding steady.
- Creatinine 1.55. This is higher again (1.31 last October, 1.42 in April). Diabetes and blood pressure over many years are the usual reasons. I'd like to recheck in about 3 months, and if it keeps rising we'll get a kidney specialist involved.
- A1c 9.2.
- Cholesterol fine, urine protein normal.
Please avoid ibuprofen/naproxen-type pain relievers; acetaminophen is fine.

documents.title: Nurse Visit: Flu Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose influenza vaccine 0.7 mL IM R deltoid. Screening questions answered no. VIS given. Observed 15 min, no reaction. FIT kit from August still not returned; reminded.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Diabetes / Kidney Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Feels well. Booster at the pharmacy last month, sore arm only. B12 monthly at home. Walking less now that it's dark early. Sugars ~170-230 fasting. No lows. No NSAIDs. No urinary symptoms, no swelling.

O: vitals reviewed. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema. Feet intact.

Labs today (called in this afternoon): creatinine 1.74, continuing to rise (1.18 at joining, 1.55 in August). A1c 9.5.

A/P:
1. Rising creatinine with long-standing diabetes and hypertension: referring to nephrology for evaluation. Continue lisinopril. Avoid NSAIDs.
2. DM2: A1c 9.5. Recommended again raising glargine; he says he'll "think about it after the holidays." Documented.
3. B12 deficiency: stable on monthly IM.
RTC after nephrology visit.

documents.title: Kidney specialist appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hello Mr. Hall, your nephrology (kidney) appointment is scheduled for Friday January 21 at 10:20 am at the outside nephrology group's office. They will mail you a new patient packet. Please bring your medication list. Call us if you need to change it.
